gaps.sentence: The lecture was dull; ___, the students stayed awake out of politeness.
___ the weather improves, the crossing will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: Unless = if the weather doesn't improve — matching the cancellation.

gaps.sentence: Insure the camera ___ it gets damaged in transit.
gaps.explanation: 'In case it gets damaged' = as a precaution against damage.

gaps.sentence: I'll take the job ___ they don't offer me any more money.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a future possibility that will not change the decision.

gaps.sentence: The match went ahead ___ the pouring rain.
gaps.explanation: Despite + noun phrase; 'although the rain' would need a clause (although it was raining).

gaps.sentence: She is not only a gifted violinist ___ a composer of some note.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only A but also B' joins the two parallel noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: ___ I thoroughly enjoyed the novel, the sequel left me cold.
gaps.explanation: Concessive 'while' = although, introducing the clause of concession.
